For k=1, e^t b_2 is asymptotic to (C^2/2)t by the exact source term. Reflection covers the other consensus. value.rationale: The motivating article explicitly asks for quantitative decay for the multi-opinion system. This resolves the exact leading exponent for every k in any known extreme-consensus basin, establishes nonzero amplitudes rather than upper bounds, and identifies a striking full-spectrum disparity: near-consensus dissent is the slow mode while more distant minorities die by a factorially ordered polynomial-exponential cascade. At k=1 an exact resonant coefficient replaces the generic k>=2 result. Opinion-class tail populations and the final approach to consensus are natural observables motivated directly by this model, not arbitrary slices. This does not solve the separate all-initial-data basin problem.
